You can reply to this post with the lengths you want for your contracts, between 1-5 years for each. This is due Tuesday at noon.

For the new guys, here are a couple of tips for contracts (my opinions only):
- You usually want to go 5 years on rookies if you're going to keep them.
- Be careful about long contracts on expensive players. There are cap penalties for dropping players, and the longer the contract the higher the penalty. A good rule of thumb is that if the contract is more than 2 years, you will need to have additional cap space beyond what the player is taking up in order to drop them. If you ever want to see what the cap hit would be on a certain contract, there is a calculator on the tab labeled "Contracts". Or you can just ask if you're not sure.
- You can cut rookies before assigning them a contract with no cap hit. For other free agents, you need to assign at least a one year deal before cutting them, which would incur a cap hit.

Blind bid waivers will process Wed. night at 11pm (this will happen every Wed. night during the season). After waivers process you can sign any free agents for $1 until noon Sunday (assuming they haven't had their game yet).

NOTE: The blind bidding uses a conditional bidding system. You are responsible for understanding how it works. If you're not sure about something, post the question here and we'll try to clarify.

Dates and times are on the league calendar as well: https://www53.myfantasyleague.com/2020/home/48571#4

Does anyone have interest in allowing adds/drops until the player’s game has started?
I’m just thinking about COVID-19 and how a player might not be on the injury report all week, but we find out when they announce inactives that they won’t play. With the ability to add someone up until their kickoff, we’d be able to pick up their backup or someone else who is playing in the game. What do you think?
